(PhysOrg.com) -- A study published Nov. 12 in the journal Nature reveals that the size and energy of the eruptions in the Sun's largest flares can vary widely, and that the flares' power might be related to their size.

The research team analyzed all of the observations of erupting flares from the Solar Dynamics Observatory (SDO) and the Coronal Mass Ejection (CME), or "space hurricane," study. The team, led by scientists from NASA's Goddard Space Flight Center in Greenbelt, Md., was able to trace the evolution of the eruptions and determine their power by comparing the scale and behavior of the flares to the scale and behavior of the Earth's magnetic field.
